findings.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Secret or API Token

cwe.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwe.description: Storing API tokens, private keys, database passwords, or JWT secrets directly in source code risks exposure via version control.

findings.description: Hardcoded API secret or credential variable assignment
findings.remediation: Load sensitive credentials exclusively from environment variables or secure secret managers (e.g., `os.environ.get('API_SECRET')`).

findings.title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized Formatted Query

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwe.description: Dynamic construction of SQL query strings using string formatting or concatenation enables unauthorized database access or modification.

findings.description: SQL query constructed using tainted variable `query` (f-string).
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries with prepared statements (e.g. `cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))`) instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via Shell Execution

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
cwe.description: Executing system commands via `os.system` or `subprocess` with `shell=True` allows attackers to append arbitrary shell operators and execute unauthorized code.

findings.description: os.system or os.popen invoked with dynamic input.
findings.remediation: Pass arguments as an explicit sequence/list to `subprocess.run([...], shell=False)` and validate inputs with strict whitelists.

findings.title: Insecure Object Deserialization

cwe.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
cwe.description: Unpickling or unsafe YAML loading from untrusted sources enables arbitrary remote code execution via custom `__reduce__` exploit payloads.

findings.remediation: Use safe serialization formats such as JSON (`json.loads`) or `yaml.safe_load`. Avoid `pickle.loads` on unauthenticated data.

findings.title: Weak Cryptographic Hash Algorithm

cwe.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
cwe.description: Using MD5 or SHA1 for security hashing or password verification is vulnerable to collision attacks and rainbow table precomputation.

findings.description: hashlib.md5 is cryptographically weak for secure operations.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to SHA-256 (`hashlib.sha256`), SHA-3, or password-specific key derivation functions such as Argon2id or bcrypt.

findings.title: Cryptographically Insecure Pseudorandom Number Generator

cwe.name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
cwe.description: The standard `random` module uses the Mersenne Twister algorithm, which is completely predictable after observing 624 outputs and unsafe for security tokens.

findings.description: random.randint is a predictable PRNG unsafe for security tokens.
findings.remediation: Use Python's `secrets` module (`secrets.token_hex`, `secrets.token_urlsafe`) for generating secure tokens, salts, and session IDs.

findings.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation via eval/exec

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
cwe.description: Using `eval()`, `exec()`, or `compile()` with user-influenced expressions allows arbitrary code execution in the running process context.

findings.description: Using `eval()`, `exec()`, or `compile()` with user-influenced expressions allows arbitrary code execution in the running process context.
findings.remediation: Refactor to use safe dispatch mappings (dictionaries), `ast.literal_eval` for literals, or domain-specific parsers.

threat_model.threat: Spoofing threat detected across 2 entry point(s). Impersonating an identity, user, or trusted service.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Enforce strong authentication, cryptographically secure randomness, and externalized secrets.

threat_model.threat: Tampering threat detected across 2 entry point(s). Unauthorized modification of database records, code, or memory.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Use parameterized queries, immutable data structures, and safe serialization.

threat_model.threat: Repudiation threat detected across 2 entry point(s). Inability to prove that an actor performed a malicious transaction.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Implement structured tamper-evident audit logging and trace IDs.

threat_model.threat: Information Disclosure threat detected across 1 entry point(s). Exposing confidential business data, tokens, or system files to unauthorized parties.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Enforce strict path canonicalization, secret manager integration, and restrictive CORS.

threat_model.threat: Denial of Service threat detected across 2 entry point(s). Degrading system availability or causing process crashes through malformed input.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Implement request timeouts, rate limiting, and safe isolated evaluators.

threat_model.threat: Elevation of Privilege threat detected across 2 entry point(s). Gaining unauthorized root, administrator, or underlying OS shell permissions.
threat_model.mitigation_strategy: Eliminate shell=True invocations, avoid dynamic eval, and run services in restricted containers.

patches.patched_code: subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", str(f"ping -c 1 {hostname}").split()[-1] if " " in str(f"ping -c 1 {hostname}") else str(f"ping -c 1 {hostname}")], check=False)

--- a/app.py
+++ b/app.py
